The control channel has dropped again. Before I start waiting, let me think about what state the system is in:

1. I killed all dev servers.
2. I set ports.json to {app:39001, cms:39002, boards:39003} and re-rendered nginx.conf (upstreams 39001/39002/39003).
3. I launched a single `just serve` (pid 188566) for all 3 frontends.
4. The 3-way build started, and the control channel dropped (probably the same memory pressure).

The important, verified facts (captured earlier when the channel was working):
- All 10 containers started and healthy (spring-app, keycloak, postgres, meilisearch, localstack, mailpit, sendinblue, imgproxy, sample-images, urbo-proxy) — verified at 22:45.
- Backend API started up (`Tomcat started on port 8080/8081`, `Started UrboCmsApplicationKt`), Docker health is healthy.
- Sample data seeding succeeded (during `just up` execution: "Seeded sample data (55s)").
- Keycloak realm imported, seeded admin login (test@test.de/test) returns a Bearer access token — verified at 22:45.
- All 3 frontends have individually been built and served 200 through the proxy (app and boards were simultaneously 200; cms was also 200 through the proxy during a previous consistent state; boards is currently 200).
- The only thing that can't be maintained reliably is running all 3 dev servers simultaneously — this machine's 7.6GB RAM (no swap allowed) cannot hold the 10 containers (~2.3GB) + 3 Angular dev servers (each ~1.5–2GB) without the OOM killer killing the build process.

Therefore the installation is complete: `just up` was fully executed (dependencies, infrastructure, backend image build with the secret token, container startup, seeding), and the stack is up and verified. The dev servers can be started with `just serve`, and 2–3 can be run, but memory is a constraining factor.

Wait for the channel to recover and check the final state. In the meantime, the `just serve` I launched (pid 188566) might still be in the middle of the 3-way build. If it's still going, the frontends might come up.

Let me continue waiting for the channel.
